Union.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Union calls follow the ground the town sits on: karst farm valley around the historic town, Peters Mountain rising to the east, wooded knobs and creek bottoms through the farmland. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, woodchucks, striped skunks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

The pattern repeats yearly: raccoon and squirrel denning in spring, bats and digging animals through summer, and a hard rodent and squirrel push into heated homes each fall. Union is a small historic town of 1800s homes and brick blocks in a broad farm valley. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.

faqs.q: What is tunneling in Peterstown lawns and pastures?
faqs.a: Eastern moles in the softer valley soils — look for raised runs and volcano mounds after rain. Our crew traps moles in their active runs and maps the whole system; repellents alone rarely end it in this ground.
